Grilling session settled eight queue decisions, recorded in tracker commit d254413. Item 151 gets a context instrument (logging sessionID, has, turn counter) with a pre-registered decision rule; 145 drops to an unattended restart since background_compaction already fires; 147 closed as done (inject_profile.rs already asserts fourth heading/position with exact query_vector); 28 §11 closed as superseded and §2–§8 delegated to syseng rehearsal; 152 treats live count as corroboration with asymmetric reading; 155 closed at test level with live reading as ceiling. Remaining owner action: one restart, then 145 runbook, 152 note read, 151 premise read.

Tags: rust, debugging, measurement, compaction

GRILLING RULINGS (2026-11-25, owner, commit d254413) for the remaining queue — eight decisions, all owner-accepted:
(1) 151's instrument rides the SAME build as the next restart, so one restart serves 145's runbook, 152's note reader, 155's ceiling and 151's premise; the counter-argument (145's run no longer on the baseline's graph) was weighed and accepted as bounded, because 145's Q1 calibration (`inject.received` status:"ok", non-zero block_bytes) goes red at the first child if the instrument disturbs anything.
(2) 151's context instrument logs THREE fields: sessionID, contexts.has(sessionID), and `turns.get(sessionID) ?? 0`. `has` alone cannot separate "no prompt ever" (the real gap) from "prompt fired, empty-success cleared the cache" (issue 155's deliberate purge); turnIndex===0 is the discriminator the premise needs. DECISION RULE PRE-REGISTERED: close 151 as measurement-not-deliverable if every `has===false` context event carries turnIndex>0; open the fallback design only on a `has===false, turnIndex===0` event.
(3) The logger is INJECTED, not imported: `registerV2Adapter(ctx, legacyHooks, { log })` with a no-op default, and v2/plugin.js passes `OPENCODE_MEM_DEBUG_INJECT === "1" ? logInfo : undefined`. Rationale: importing plugin.js back into adapter.js closes the cycle that plugin.js:1945-1950 protects; and deciding the flag at the call site makes flag-off a CODE PATH (`if (log)`) instead of an env read, so absence is a plain unit test — issue 153's own rule that default-off absence is enforced in the harness, not assumed from the caller's environment.
(4) 145's runbook: compaction is taken OFF the owner's list. `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc:9` has experimental.background_compaction:true, compaction is DETECTABLE after the fact via Q0 (`type='compaction'` rows), and Q6's only real constraint is that the nonce be written AFTER the boundary — not that the boundary be predicted. Owner's action reduces to the restart. Pre-registered fallback: if fewer than N children show a compaction row inside a bounded window, record `OPEN — no compaction observed` and ask for one manual `/compact` each.
(5) 28's §11 live swap is CLOSED AS SUPERSEDED, not deferred: opencode.jsonc:216-220 already lists the local plugin and holds no opencode-mem reference, and the live root carries the migrator's .bak marker, so the step describes the current world; repeating it would redo a completed migration on the only copy of the user's memory, which the issue's own 2026-10-29 ruling forbids. AC2 closes on the ruling. §2–§8 (copy-first) stays in scope and is delegated to a subagent.
(6) 147 CLOSED as done with AC-3's residual RECLASSIFIED from "owner must accept a gap" to covered-by: `crates/mem-bridge/tests/inject_profile.rs` renders a block and asserts `## Related older sessions` is present AND ordered (recent_at < older_at < history_close_at), and `inject_relevance.rs` pins the scored arm — both with the exact `query_vector: Some` the probe's `query_chars:0` cannot produce. Stronger than a probe would be. Step 8 (vi) moves BLOCKED→covered-by.
(7) 152's post-fix live check is CORROBORATION WITH AN ASYMMETRIC READING, never a pass condition: non-zero `[pid ` rows are informative on their own; ZERO is uninformative because the escaping ceiling still holds (quote/newline commands never match), and the exit condition is a session holding a short quote-free command (e.g. `echo marker-…-$(date +%s)`) — if such a session still yields no note, THAT is the defect.
(8) 155 CLOSES AT TEST LEVEL with the live observation named a CEILING, not a debt: producing a live refresh failure requires breaking the engine mid-turn on the owner's store, so the observation is unobtainable except by sabotage; the rule is pinned by a mutant (reinstating the pre-call delete reds the amended v2-memory-context pin) and the transport half by 162's wire criteria.
LESSON: two "owner must accept a residual" lines in this queue (147's AC-3) described gaps that did not exist on inspection — accepting residuals without checking them is how defects survive a green suite.

Agreed to close issue 155 (keep-on-failure) at test level rather than keep it open as debt. The behavior — failed refresh keeps the cached block it could not replace — is pinned by the amended v2-memory-context test, which reds when the pre-call delete is reinstated (mutant discrimination). A live observation is permanently unobservable because producing it requires breaking the engine mid-turn; the transport half is separately pinned by injectStatus and issue 162's two wire criteria. Recorded as a ceiling, following issue 163's precedent of ceilings for escaped commands and double-stamping.

Tags: memory-context, testing, issue-tracking, ceiling

Q6 was recorded. For issue 152, the proposed Q7 pass condition avoids gating closure on the live `[pid ` count because JSON escaping can make zero uninformative; instead, treat a non-zero count as positive end-to-end evidence and a zero as meaningful only when a known short, escape-free command is present for falsification.

Tags: issue-152, debugging, test-criteria, logging

Issue 147 closure discussion: AC-3's residual is already covered by crate tests (`inject_profile.rs` asserts the `## Related older sessions` heading and ordering, and `inject_relevance.rs` pins the scored arm), so close as done and reclassify the residual as covered elsewhere rather than treating it as an evidence gap. An optional live `inject.received` reading remains if runtime proof is wanted.

Tags: issue-147, testing, memory-injection, ac-3

Investigated the live migration state for the Rust port of opencode-agents-memory. Confirmed the TS→Rust swap already occurred: ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc (lines 216-220) lists the local plugin/ with no opencode-mem reference, and the live root carries user-profiles.db.schema-v1-*.bak migrator rename markers. Raised Q5 on issue #28 (parity): whether §11's live repeat (which closes AC2) should be closed as superseded by the live system rather than re-run. Recommended closing §11 as superseded and delegating §2-§8 against a copy on port 3749, because repeating the swap would risk the only copy of user memory to re-prove a completed migration; the owner ruling forbids using the live root as a test fixture. Trade-off noted: no contemporaneous before/after transcript of the swap itself would exist, only evidence that the port runs and is migratable.

Tags: rust, migration, parity, opencode-mem

Advanced planning for runbook 145. Q3's recommendation was accepted. Q4 challenges whether the owner must manually trigger compaction in each of the five children, proposing instead to rely on background_compaction=true in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc and detect compaction boundaries afterward using Q0's max(seq) query for type='compaction'. The proposal keeps the nonce-after-boundary constraint intact while reducing owner effort to a restart, with a fallback to manual /compact if too few children show compaction rows within a bounded window.

Tags: runbook-145, compaction, background-compaction, experiment

Q3 decision: the context line reaches the log via an optional `log` injected into `registerV2Adapter(ctx, legacyHooks, { log })` (defaulting to a no-op), with the `OPENCODE_MEM_DEBUG_INJECT` flag evaluated at the call site in `v2/plugin.js`. This avoids an import cycle (adapter.js imports only legacy-client.js), keeps the flag reader-side where plugin.js:271 already reads it, and makes the flag-off case a testable `if (log)` code path instead of environment-dependent module loading. Rejected alternative: adapter pushing to a shared array drained by plugin.js.

Tags: adapter, logging, architecture, plugin

Determined that a query-less inject does produce a block: inject.rs tiers search_memories_by_content when a query exists and list_memories_by_container_tag otherwise, so 'no query' degrades to the tag list rather than nothing; the block: None at inject.rs:7-10 reflects absent project_id policy, not query. For issue 151, recommended that the context-hook instrument also log the session turn counter (turns.get(event.sessionID) ?? 0 from adapter.js:22-23) alongside sessionID and contexts.has(sessionID), because has() alone cannot distinguish a never-prompted session (real gap) from a cache cleared by an empty-success purge (working as designed after issue 155). Proposed pre-registered decision rule: close 151 as measurement if all has===false events have turnIndex>0; open fallback design only on a has===false, turnIndex===0 event.

Tags: context-hook, memory-inject, instrumentation, session-cache

Grilling session on remaining sequencing decisions for the opencode-agents-memory project. Measured that since the 22:47:45 restart, 14 sessions had host messages and all 14 carried an inject.requested; across the whole log, 142 sessions carry an inject line matching 142 distinct ids, so no session ran without the prompt path. The context hook cannot log context events, so never-prompted children remain invisible. Q1 posed to user: whether issue 151's instrument (a log line in the context hook within plugin/src/v2/adapter.js) should ride the same build as the next restart alongside issues 145/152/155, or wait until 145's runbook reports. Recommendation is same build, since restarts are the scarce owner-held action and the instrument cannot disturb 145 readings (failure surfaces immediately via inject.received status/block_bytes). Counter-argument: a build adding an instrument mid-measurement wave means 145 results can no longer be compared to the earlier baseline. Awaiting user decision.

Tags: instrumentation, debugging, session-management, plugin

CLOSED issue 153 (2026-11-25, commit 8ae56ea) on a MEASURED flag-on reading, not an inference: OPENCODE_MEM_DEBUG_INJECT=1 IS present in the live host's environment (/proc/26479/environ, /proc/28056/environ, /proc/28648/environ), and the log splits cleanly — 144 `inject.received` lines WITHOUT `sections` (newest 2026-11-24T13:31:56.936+07:00, flag off) then 65 WITH `sections` and `block_prefix` (first 2026-11-24T13:59:04.546+07:00, newest 2026-11-25T00:11:32.713+07:00), no interleaving. Two readings begin `["Recent actions", …]`, which is issue 161's fix visible in the same telemetry. Also flipped 160 (shipped 1a97781, direct correction not a wave) and 161 (done and verified live: running engine 115bfb382d914b48, sections[0] is the block's first heading). REMAINING QUEUE — all four now owner-gated: 151 needs-info (instrument = one structured line in adapter.js's `context` hook recording sessionID + contexts.has(sessionID); wrapper change + host restart; owner approval per the issue), 147 ready-for-human (owner must accept AC-3's source-level-only verdict), 28 ready-for-human (owner-run live repeat of the 41-row rehearsal), 145 landed (M1 arm (a)/(b) gap needs the runbook docs/evidence/issue-145/README.md, which requires 5 fresh children plus OWNER-triggered compaction; its Q1 calibration passes now: 418 host_contract lines all "setup", last inject.received status ok, block_bytes non-zero, level info).

DECISION (issue 162, shipped a958667 2026-11-25, review APPROVED): the injectStatus seam now has two end-to-end cases, both in plugin/tests/v2-inject-delivery.test.mjs. (1) test_inject_status_empty_clears_a_compacted_block seeds WIRE_BLOCK, pins injects===1, asserts [] after the empty-success refresh — a never-seeded cache fails the seed assertion rather than passing for the wrong reason. (2) test_chat_message_output_hides_inject_status_from_enumeration hands a CALLER-BUILT object to the real hooks["chat.message"] and asserts BOTH Object.keys(output) omits injectStatus AND Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(output,"injectStatus").enumerable===false — the descriptor half is load-bearing because an absent field also has no key, so omission alone would go green with the producer deleted (that was the exact vacuity of the original claim about v2-plugin-adapter.test.mjs:129, which deep-compares an adapter-built output against a stub hook that never sets the field). Key correction from the gate: the earlier premise "the wrapper returns nothing so no test can hold the output" was HALF true — the adapter's internal object is unreachable, but plugin/src/plugin.js:1463-1467 annotates ANY object handed to chat.message unconditionally, so the public hook suffices. Mutant B must use the full text `{ value: injectStatus, enumerable: false }` because bare `enumerable: false` matches twice in dist/plugin.js (producer + shouldRefresh). Harness knob injectModePath (default null, helloConfigPath idiom) must be read BEFORE the injectMode==="error" branch, or the per-request re-read cannot reach the error path; wireRun actually stages injectMode "block" so the fixture transition is block→empty-success, not error→empty — `success` is an unnamed fallthrough to { block: null }, a suite convention used at three call sites, and needs no named branch. Production untouched: no plugin/src, no plugin/dist, no crates change. Still NOT live-observed: issue 155's keep-on-failure path.

Independently re-ran all acceptance criteria: C2 descriptor assertion on the same caller-built object, C1 wire criterion seeds/pins/asserts empty cache; applied mutants B and C with trap/cp/cmp restore and confirmed AssertionError REDs; verified harness injectModePath default inert and injectMode let; confirmed production untouched (plugin/src, plugin/dist, crates); recorded block->success discrepancy; ran dist-sync suites. Wrote review deliverable APPROVED.

Tags: review, testing, inject-status, plugin

Investigated a discrepancy in bpf(2) syscall errno behavior for the attr size parameter on kernel 6.18.64_1. The executor's probe reported size=4096→EFAULT while the live probe showed E2BIG. Cross-checked binaries, disassembly, and rebuilt the exact source; determined the upper-bound errno is buffer-placement-sensitive (global .data crossing pages → EFAULT; heap/stack → E2BIG ≥256; 153–160 EINVAL placement-sensitive). The two guard-pinned boundaries are stable across all placements: 152 → EBADFD and 0 → EINVAL. Wrote the review verdict (APPROVED) and corrected a banked memory gotcha that had recorded size=4096→EFAULT as unconditional.

Tags: bpf, kernel, syscall, errno
